issues.display_title: Issue #423: Create User Social Links Table
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 06/08/26

✅ Implementation: Create User Social Links Table

DDL

CREATE TABLE user_social_links (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    type TEXT NOT NULL,
    url TEXT NOT NULL,
    position SMALLINT NOT NULL CHECK (position BETWEEN 1 AND 10),
    created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UNIQUE (user_id, position)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_user_social_links_user_id ON user_social_links(user_id);

Model

Added Models.UserSocialLink mapped to user_social_links with UUID ownership, resolved link type, URL, position, and timestamps.

Constraints

  • User deletion cascades to social links.
  • Position is restricted to 1-10.
  • Position is unique per user.
  • Link type duplicates remain allowed.
  • User index supports ordered profile lookup.

Verification

go test ./src/Action/V2/Users ./src/Routes/V2 -count=1
go test ./... -count=1
git diff --check

Scope

  • Create user_social_links with UUID primary key and user ownership.
  • Store resolved link type and URL as TEXT.
  • Restrict positions to 1-10 and make each user-position unique.
  • Cascade-delete links when a user is deleted.
  • Add user lookup index and GORM model.

DDL

CREATE TABLE user_social_links (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    type TEXT NOT NULL,
    url TEXT NOT NULL,
    position SMALLINT NOT NULL CHECK (position BETWEEN 1 AND 10),
    created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UNIQUE (user_id, position)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_user_social_links_user_id ON user_social_links(user_id);

RESULT 06/08/26

✅ Implementation: API Edit Profile V2

Route

PATCH /v2/users/me/profile
Authorization: <JWT token>
Content-Type: application/json

Payload

{
  "username": "ipebbbbb",
  "fullname": "Pebi Sandi P",
  "about": "Exploring the world in 360°.",
  "country": "Indonesia",
  "city": "Bandung",
  "website": "linktr.ee/ipebbbbb"
}

Omitted fields remain unchanged. Country and city must be populated after update. Website normalizes to HTTPS.

Success

{"statusCode":200,"data":{"valid":true,"messages":"Success update profile"}}

Changes

  • Added V2 action, controller, and PATCH route.
  • Reused legacy username/fullname validation behavior.
  • Added about, country, city, and website validation.
  • Added Redis refresh, Elasticsearch username update, and live Maps Panorra sync.
  • No encrypted response.

Errors

  • 400: invalid JSON.
  • 401: invalid auth or role.
  • 409: user missing or username conflict.
  • 422: invalid fields or missing final country/city.
  • 500: database or downstream sync failure.

Endpoint

PATCH /v2/users/me/profile

Scope

  • Update username, fullname, about, country, city, and website.
  • Keep omitted PATCH fields unchanged.
  • Require non-empty country and city after update.
  • Follow legacy username/fullname validation.
  • Limit about to 2200 characters.
  • Normalize website to HTTPS and limit it to 100 characters.
  • Refresh Redis; update Elasticsearch for username changes; sync Maps Panorra on live for username/fullname changes.
  • Return common statusCode/data success envelope without encryption.

RESULT 06/08/26

✅ Implementation: Update API Social Links

Route

PUT /v2/users/me/social
Authorization: <JWT token>
Content-Type: application/json

Payload

{
  "links": [
    {"type": "instagram", "url": "instagram.com/raka"},
    {"url": "youtube.com/@raka"},
    {"type": "unknown", "url": "portfolio.example.com"}
  ]
}

Behavior

  • Replaces full list inside one database transaction.
  • Empty array deletes all links.
  • Maximum 10; duplicate link types allowed.
  • Array order becomes position 1-10.
  • URLs normalize to HTTPS; maximum 2048 characters.
  • Recognized optional type is used directly.
  • Unknown or absent type triggers domain detection.
  • Unknown domains default to website.

Supported platforms: Instagram, Facebook, X/Twitter, LinkedIn, TikTok, YouTube.
Resolved value is persisted in user_social_links.type; unknown domains use website.

Success

{"statusCode":200,"data":{"valid":true,"messages":"Success update social links"}}

Errors

  • 400: invalid JSON.
  • 401: invalid auth or role.
  • 409: user missing.
  • 422: more than 10 links or invalid URL.
  • 500: transaction failure.

Endpoint

PUT /v2/users/me/social

Scope

  • Replace the authenticated user's complete social-link list atomically.
  • Accept maximum 10 links; empty array removes all links.
  • Accept optional type: Instagram, Facebook, X/Twitter, LinkedIn, TikTok, YouTube, or website.
  • Use a recognized submitted type directly; ignore unknown types and detect from URL domain.
  • Default to website when neither submitted type nor URL domain is recognized.
  • Normalize URLs to HTTPS and limit each URL to 2048 characters.
  • Persist resolved value in user_social_links.type.
  • Allow duplicate link types.
  • Assign position 1-10 from array order.
  • Return common statusCode/data success envelope without encryption.

issues.display_title: Issue #427: API: Add Audit Trail for Register and Login Activity
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 06/08/26

✅ Implementation: Register and Login Activity Audit

Summary

Implemented non-blocking audit logging for email, Google, and Apple register/login activity. The audit wrapper runs after each auth handler, derives success from the final HTTP status, and records request metadata without storing credentials or request bodies.

Database

DDL: migrations/20260806_create_user_activity_logs.sql.

Table stores event type, optional user/encrypt/provider/failure reason, request metadata, JSONB metadata, and timestamp. Indexes cover user, event type, device, and descending time.

DDL

CREATE TABLE user_activity_logs (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id UUID NULL,
    encrypt TEXT NULL,
    event_type TEXT NOT NULL,
    auth_provider TEXT NULL,
    success BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
    failure_reason TEXT NULL,
    ip_address TEXT NULL,
    user_agent TEXT NULL,
    device_id TEXT NULL,
    device_name TEXT NULL,
    platform TEXT NULL,
    app_version TEXT NULL,
    os_version TEXT NULL,
    app_build TEXT NULL,
    request_path TEXT NULL,
    metadata JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_user_activity_logs_user_id_created_at
    ON user_activity_logs(user_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_user_activity_logs_event_type_created_at
    ON user_activity_logs(event_type, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_user_activity_logs_device_id_created_at
    ON user_activity_logs(device_id, created_at DESC);

Backend

  • Models.UserActivityLog maps the audit table.
  • ActivityLog.ExtractRequestMetadata reads IP, user agent, device, platform, app, OS, build, and path.
  • ActivityLog.Record writes a row.
  • ActivityLog.RecordNonBlocking logs write failures without failing auth.
  • ActivityLog.Wrap records route outcome after handler execution.
  • ActivityLog.SetUserContext adds user context when handlers resolve/create a user.

Integrated providers: email, Google, Apple. Events: register_success, register_failed, login_success, login_failed.

Integrated Routes

Route Provider Success event Failure event
POST /register/user email register_success register_failed
POST /register/google google register_success register_failed
POST /register/apple apple register_success register_failed
POST /auth email login_success login_failed
POST /auth/google google login_success login_failed
POST /auth/apple apple login_success login_failed

POST /auth/viewer and POST /register/validate are excluded because neither represents a requested account register/login event.

Processing Flow

  1. Route invokes the existing auth handler through ActivityLog.Wrap.
  2. Handler runs normally and preserves its existing response.
  3. When the handler resolves or creates a user, SetUserContext stores user_id and encrypt in request-local state.
  4. Wrapper reads the final HTTP status. Status below 400 records success; status 400+ or handler error records failure.
  5. Wrapper extracts request metadata and calls RecordNonBlocking.
  6. Database write failure is logged with the event type, then the original auth response continues unchanged.

Failure reason contains only the standard HTTP status text, such as Bad Request or Unauthorized. It never copies the raw request or response body.

Headers

X-Device-Id
X-Device-Name
X-Platform
X-App-Version
X-OS-Version
X-App-Build
User-Agent

Example request:

POST /auth
Content-Type: application/json
User-Agent: Panorra/2.0
X-Device-Id: 6947bf28-40dd-4f96-b477-e4cda77ac917
X-Device-Name: iPhone 15 Pro
X-Platform: ios
X-App-Version: 2.0.0
X-OS-Version: 18.0
X-App-Build: 200

X-Platform accepts ios, android, and web case-insensitively. Missing or unsupported values are stored as unknown.

Stored Row Examples

Successful Google login:

{
  "event_type": "login_success",
  "user_id": "47091c14-1218-4f6f-9b81-85d5e6ea4cb6",
  "encrypt": "ecabc12345",
  "auth_provider": "google",
  "success": true,
  "failure_reason": null,
  "platform": "ios",
  "request_path": "/auth/google",
  "metadata": {}
}

Failed email login before user resolution:

{
  "event_type": "login_failed",
  "user_id": null,
  "encrypt": null,
  "auth_provider": "email",
  "success": false,
  "failure_reason": "Bad Request",
  "platform": "web",
  "request_path": "/auth",
  "metadata": {}
}

Security Boundaries

Never stored:

  • Password or password hash from the request.
  • JWT, OAuth token, Apple token, refresh token, or authorization header.
  • OTP or captcha value.
  • Raw request or response body.
  • Raw email for failed-login analytics.

The metadata field currently receives an empty object and exists only for safe future expansion.

Files Changed

  • migrations/20260806_create_user_activity_logs.sql
  • src/Models/UserActivityLog.go
  • src/Utils/ActivityLog/ActivityLog.go
  • src/Utils/ActivityLog/ActivityLog_test.go
  • src/Routes/V1/AuthRoutes.go
  • src/Routes/V1/RegisterRoutes.go
  • Email, Google, and Apple auth/register actions for resolved user context.
  • api-collection/Panorra API Post/Auth/folder.yml

Verification

go test ./src/Utils/ActivityLog ./src/Routes/V1 ./src/Action/V1/Auth ./src/Action/V1/Register -count=1
go test ./... -count=1
git diff --check

API: Add audit trail for register and login activity

Context

We need an internal analytics/audit trail for user account events, starting with register and login. The goal is to capture useful internal data such as login device, platform, app version, IP address, and user agent so the team can understand user sessions and authentication activity.

Current repo findings:

  • This Go API repo has JWT auth middleware and user lookup helpers.
  • It has GET /check-token and GET /check-auth.
  • It stores user_detail.last_login and exposes user data through Redis-backed helpers.
  • The actual register/login handlers do not appear to be in this repo, so this task should create reusable audit-log infrastructure that the register/login service can call, or can be wired in here if those flows are added later.

Scope

Create backend support for recording register/login activity events.

Initial event types:

  • register_success
  • register_failed
  • login_success
  • login_failed

Data To Capture

Each audit event should capture:

  • event_type
  • user_id when available
  • encrypt when available
  • auth_provider, for example email, google, facebook, apple
  • success
  • failure_reason when applicable
  • ip_address
  • user_agent
  • device_id
  • device_name
  • platform, for example ios, android, web, unknown
  • app_version
  • os_version
  • app_build
  • request_path
  • metadata as JSONB for safe future expansion
  • created_at

Recommended client headers:

X-Device-Id
X-Device-Name
X-Platform
X-App-Version
X-OS-Version
X-App-Build
User-Agent

Proposed Schema

CREATE TABLE user_activity_logs (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id UUID NULL,
  encrypt TEXT NULL,
  event_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  auth_provider TEXT NULL,
  success BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
  failure_reason TEXT NULL,
  ip_address TEXT NULL,
  user_agent TEXT NULL,
  device_id TEXT NULL,
  device_name TEXT NULL,
  platform TEXT NULL,
  app_version TEXT NULL,
  os_version TEXT NULL,
  app_build TEXT NULL,
  request_path TEXT NULL,
  metadata JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

Recommended indexes:

CREATE INDEX idx_user_activity_logs_user_id_created_at ON user_activity_logs(user_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_user_activity_logs_event_type_created_at ON user_activity_logs(event_type, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_user_activity_logs_device_id_created_at ON user_activity_logs(device_id, created_at DESC);

Implementation Notes

  • Add a reusable model/helper for creating activity-log rows.
  • Add a small request metadata extractor that reads IP, user agent, and the recommended device/app headers from fiber.Ctx.
  • Do not block register/login success if audit logging fails; log the error and continue.
  • Avoid storing passwords, tokens, OTP values, raw request bodies, or other sensitive authentication secrets.
  • If email is needed for failed login analytics, prefer storing a normalized email hash rather than raw email.
  • Keep the first version focused on register/login only. Full API activity logging can be a later task.

Acceptance Criteria

  • user_activity_logs table schema is defined and ready to apply.
  • Backend has a reusable function for recording register/login audit events.
  • Backend captures device/app metadata from request headers.
  • Register/login success and failure events can be recorded with user context when available.
  • Audit logging failures do not break the user-facing auth flow.
  • Sensitive values such as passwords, tokens, OTPs, and raw request bodies are never stored.
  • Basic indexes support querying by user, event type, device, and time.
  • API collection or documentation includes the expected client headers for mobile/frontend.

Future Follow-Up

After register/login audit logging is in place, create a separate task for broader authenticated API activity logging and internal analytics dashboards.

RESULT 06/08/26

✅ Implementation: Delete Avatar V2

Summary

Extended the existing Upload Avatar V2 endpoint with avatar deletion. An explicitly submitted empty multipart text field selects deletion; omitted fields remain invalid and file fields continue through upload.

API Contract

Route

PUT /v2/users/me/avatar
Authorization: <JWT token>
Content-Type: multipart/form-data

Delete Payload

avatar=
ec=false

Example:

curl --request PUT "{{base_url}}/v2/users/me/avatar" \
  --header "Authorization: <JWT token>" \
  --form-string "avatar=" \
  --form "ec=false"

The avatar part must be a text field. An empty file field remains part of the upload validation flow.

Plain Success Response

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "messages": "Success delete avatar",
    "avatar": null
  }
}

With ec=true, the same response envelope is encrypted using the existing flow and returned as cry with ls.

No Existing Avatar

Status: 422 Unprocessable Entity

{
  "statusCode": 422,
  "data": {
    "status": "Unprocessable Entity",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Avatar not found",
      "input": "avatar"
    }
  }
}

Processing Flow

  1. Authenticate the user and load the stored avatar and local path.
  2. Inspect parsed multipart text values. Only an explicitly present empty avatar text value selects deletion.
  3. Reject deletion when either stored avatar or path is absent or empty.
  4. Initialize MinIO and delete the object using the base name of the stored path.
  5. Delete the local file. Ignore os.IsNotExist; return HTTP 500 for other errors.
  6. Set database fields avatar and path to SQL NULL, then update updated_at.
  7. Refresh Redis and run Maps Panorra synchronization when PREFIX=live.
  8. Return the plain or encrypted success response.

Changes Applied

  • src/Action/V2/Users/UploadAvatar.go
    • Added avatarDeleteRequested to distinguish empty text input from missing and file inputs.
    • Added MinIO, local-file, database, cache, synchronization, and response handling for deletion.
  • src/Action/V2/Users/UploadAvatar_test.go
    • Verifies explicit empty text selects deletion.
    • Verifies missing and file fields do not select deletion.

Error Handling

  • No stored avatar or path: HTTP 422, Avatar not found.
  • MinIO client failure: HTTP 500, Failed to initialize MinIO client.
  • MinIO deletion failure: HTTP 500, Failed to delete avatar.
  • Local deletion failure other than missing file: HTTP 500, Failed to delete avatar file.
  • Database or encryption failure: HTTP 500, Internal Server Error.

Verification

go test ./src/Action/V2/Users -run TestAvatarDeleteRequested -count=1
go test ./... -count=1
git diff --check

Results:

  • Request-classification tests passed.
  • Full Go test suite passed.
  • Diff whitespace check passed.

Background

PUT /v2/users/me/avatar only handled multipart file uploads. Clients need to remove an existing avatar through the same endpoint by sending an explicitly empty text field.

Objective

Treat multipart text field avatar="" as a delete request without changing file upload behavior.

Scope

  • Distinguish an explicit empty text field from a missing field and a file field.
  • Return 422 Unprocessable Entity with Avatar not found when no stored avatar exists.
  • Delete the stored MinIO object and local file.
  • Set users.avatar and users.path to SQL NULL after storage cleanup succeeds.
  • Refresh Redis and sync Maps Panorra when PREFIX=live.
  • Preserve plain and encrypted response modes.
  • Add focused request-classification tests.

Constraints

  • Missing avatar remains the existing required-parameter error.
  • Multipart file avatar remains the existing upload flow.
  • A missing local file is treated as already deleted.
  • Storage failures must not clear database values.
  • Do not change the API collection file as part of this task.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Explicit multipart text avatar="" deletes an existing avatar.
  • MinIO and local files are removed before database fields are cleared.
  • Successful plain response returns 200, Success delete avatar, and avatar: null.
  • ec=true returns the existing encrypted cry and ls envelope.
  • Empty delete request without an existing avatar returns HTTP 422.
  • Missing field still returns Required Param Avatar.
  • File upload behavior is unchanged.
  • Full Go test suite passes.
